s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with seizures, hemiparesis, and developmental delays
salient_findings: Recurrent seizures starting at age 3 months
Marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres with significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere
key_facts: Age of onset of seizures: 3 months
Seizures are recurrent and progressive
Left-sided weakness is present
Developmental delays are noted
Cognitive impairment is significant
Marked left hemiparesis with brisk reflexes is present
Electroencephalography shows focal abnormal brain activity
Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrates marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres
Right cerebral hemisphere shows significant atrophy
No family history of neurological disorders
No reported perinatal complications or trauma

shortlist.label: Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by cerebral hemiatrophy, seizures, and intellectual disability, matching the patient's presentation

shortlist.label: Rasmussen encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive hemiparesis and seizures are key features, although the lack of certain diagnostic criteria may lower its likelihood

shortlist.label: Hemimegalencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Involves hemispheric malformation and can cause seizures, developmental delays, and hemiparesis, consistent with the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Although typically associated with a port-wine stain, it can cause seizures, hemiparesis, and developmental delays due to cerebral hemiatrophy

shortlist.label: Perinatal ischemic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the patient's hemiparesis and seizures, especially given the absence of a clear family history or perinatal complications

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of recurrent seizures, left-sided weakness, developmental delays, and significant cognitive impairment, combined with the brain MRI findings of marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres, significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere, and ipsilateral calvarial thickening, are consistent with Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome, which is characterized by cerebral hemiatrophy, seizures, and intellectual disability.

rejected.label: Rasmussen encephalitis
rejected.why: While Rasmussen encephalitis can cause progressive hemiparesis and seizures, it typically presents with more rapid progression and inflammation, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Hemimegalencephaly
rejected.why: Hemimegalencephaly is characterized by an enlarged cerebral hemisphere, which is not consistent with the atrophy seen in this patient's right cerebral hemisphere.

rejected.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: Sturge-Weber syndrome typically presents with a port-wine stain, which is not mentioned in this case, and is associated with leptomeningeal angiomatosis, which is not described in the MRI findings.

rejected.label: Perinatal ischemic stroke
rejected.why: Perinatal ischemic stroke could explain some of the patient's symptoms, but it would not typically cause the marked cerebral hemiatrophy and calvarial thickening seen in this case.
